The inner fi and the source refusal's closing brace are indented, so the first column-0 fi closes the guard. Each block must name its own installer exactly twice (:391); after that path is replaced, all five must be equal (:392-393), hold no "$(" (:395), and hold the three-up helper path (:396). A copy that differs in any byte makes the set larger than one. A closing fi with trailing text extends that block to a later column-0 fi, so it differs too. The same drift in all five is caught per installer by the behaviour tests: the empty PATH case (:338-352), absent and mode-000 helpers that must exit 2 with the named path (:354-364), and a helper that returns 7 and one that does not parse (:366-379). These run copies in tempfile scratch trees (:309-329). The replace is unambiguous: no installer path contains another's. In install/, only these five call is_ci_runner (grep is_ci_runner install), so the hand-kept INSTALLERS tuple (:294-300) covers every current caller. What the pin does not assert is in the unit's hardening notes.

hardening_notes: tests/unit/test_ci_runner.py pins the guard's bytes and its absent, unreadable, failing and unparsable branches, but no case reaches the bare-name branch (`*) ci_runner_helper="../../../scripts/lib/ci-runner.sh"`, e.g. install/macos/common/brew.sh:28): every test passes a path with a slash. A case that runs `bash brew.sh` from the installer's own directory, and one from another directory, would pin that the CWD-relative fallback is right only in the first.

The block pin does not assert that the guard precedes the first is_ci_runner use in each file, or that INSTALLERS (tests/unit/test_ci_runner.py:294-300) lists every installer that calls is_ci_runner. Deriving the tuple from `grep -l is_ci_runner install/` and asserting the guard's offset is below the first call would keep a sixth installer, or a call moved above the guard, from passing unseen.
